transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-12-01 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park, Priya Shah, Carlos Mendes - Redwood; Maya Liu, Tom Rivera, Sonia Patel, Liam O'Connor, Raya Kim - Cheshire Systems

Summary (auto): Kickoff — infra intake and onboarding plan. Security questions about KMS and data residency. Network/VPC alignment and pilot scope decided.

00:00 Ethan: okay uh everyone on? good afternoon good morning depending on where you are. this is Ethan from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. thanks Maya and team for carving out time.
00:12 Maya: yeah thanks Ethan um we have a couple folks from infra and security here; I'm Maya, i'll be shepherding the program.
00:20 Tom: Tom here, infrastructure lead, quick note we have strict VPC peering rules and a bastion jump policy.
00:27 Priya: great, i'm Priya, SE at Redwood, i'll run through the architecture and pilot options. we'll try to keep it technical enough for the infra folks and high level for roadmap.
00:36 Carlos: and Carlos from CS, i'll coordinate follow-ups and the pilot schedule.
00:40 Sonia: Sonia, Security. hope to cover KMS, audit logs, retention.
00:45 Ethan: perfect. quick agenda — run 10m of what redwood looks like in hosted vs dedicated vs private, then networking and security intake, then pilot scope and success criteria, and wrap with action items.
01:02 Priya: okay slide-free for now, but to orient — Redwood exposes a unified API whether you use Hosted, Dedicated reserved capacity, or Private VPC. the customer experience and SDKs are the same; difference is where compute runs and the isolation guarantees.
01:18 Maya: can you clarify the dedicated option — is that single-tenant GPU pools or logical isolation?
01:25 Priya: it's reserved GPU pools so for Dedicated you get a capacity reservation per customer - physical tenancy is shared in some setups but network and workload isolation is enforced. Private is the VPC/on-prem shipping option with full control over network and key management.
01:39 Tom: so for Private we bring our own subnet, is that right? and we manage peering?
01:45 Ethan: yes for the Private VPC model you either peering or transit gateway; you supply the CIDR and account info. Redwood will provide a minimal port list and peering request.
01:55 Sonia: and what about KMS — can we keep our own key? we can't allow keys managed by third-party.
02:02 Priya: yep you can bring your own KMS/HSM. we integrate with customer KMS for encryption at rest keys and we can log key rotation events. occasionally the transcription will note we said "bring your own KMS" as BYOK.
02:14 Sonia: okay good. what about audit logs retention? we need 1 year retention for our logs for audits.
02:21 Carlos: we have enterprise retention packs and we can configure log export to your S3 or SIEM, that's standard.
02:27 Sonia: any chance of logs anonymization at ingest?
02:30 Priya: we have masking pipelines, but for production-grade masking for PII you'd typically run a pre-ingest scrub or use our built-in redaction filters; we'll follow up on specifics.
02:41 Liam: network-wise we need IP allowlisting for agent calls. is there a static egress set?
02:46 Ethan: for Hosted we have published egress IP ranges per region. for Private/Dedicated, egress comes from customer VPC so you control it.
02:55 Tom: good, will need that list for our security team.
03:00 Priya: i'll send the port list and egress ranges. note that if you do Dedicated + Managed egress we recommend NATed egress with firewall rules.
03:11 Maya: timeline — we're aiming for a Q1 pilot, maybe mid-jan, is that feasible?
03:16 Ethan: absolutely. pilot in mid-january aligns with our capacity planning; we'll need initial workload samples and a short prompt set to measure latency/cost and quality.
03:27 Raya: product question: what metrics should we capture for success?
03:30 Priya: look for latency p95 under your SLA threshold, token cost per 1k requests, correctness on your eval dataset — we can run model A/B tests and tie regressions to prompt sets.
03:41 Tom: about costs: we're sensitive to per-token pricing spikes. how mature are quantization options?
03:46 Priya: we do quantized variants and model recommendations with Redwood Optimize. for inference cost we suggest eval runs on a small set to see quality-vs-cost curves. i'll prepare quantization profiles.
03:58 Sonia: compliance: do you have SOC2 and ISO certs? and can you share pen test reports?
04:05 Ethan: yes we are SOC2 Type II and we can share a redacted report and a compliance pack. we'll also provide details on role-based access control and SSO/SAML config.
04:14 Sonia: good. and for data residency — we need EU-only processing for some datasets. can you pin region?
04:19 Priya: yes model routing supports region pinning; for Private you'd run in your region and for Hosted we have region options — we'll note this in the onboarding doc.
04:28 Tom: any special network ports?
04:30 Priya: minimal — mainly HTTPS (443) and a health/metrics port for optional connectivity. i'll include full list in follow-up.
04:40 Maya: okay great. let's talk about pilot scope — what kind of benchmark do you recommend?
04:46 Priya: two-phase. phase one: functional correctness and latency with a small eval set (200 prompts). phase two: throughput/p95 and KV cache stress tests using synthetic sequences matching your longest contexts.
05:00 Liam: KV cache? you mean key-value cache for chat?
05:03 Priya: yes, our runtime maintains KV cache per session for long chats - sometimes transcribed as KV cash — it matters for memory and latency.
05:11 Tom: how do you measure cold vs warm start?
05:13 Priya: we run cold-start tests (fresh instance) and warm-start with populated kvs; we'll show delta in latency graphs.
05:20 Maya: on stakeholders, i'll be exec sponsor, Tom will own infra, Sonia for security signoff, Raya will track product KPIs.
05:27 Ethan: perfect. i'll coordinate the schedule. quick question on SLA: do you need an SLA right away or just pilot-level expectations?
05:34 Maya: pilot-level for now, but if pilot goes well we'll need enterprise SLA and a dedicated contract.
05:40 Carlos: noted. we'll draft a pilot statement of work and include upgrade paths.
05:46 Tom: about ingress — are there any inbound VPC connections needed or is it outbound only?
05:52 Priya: for Private, we usually require peering or IGW routing so inbound is controlled; we'll document the flow. for Hosted it's outbound from your services into the API.
06:05 Sonia: curious about token-level billing and visibility — can we see token breakdown per route?
06:10 Ethan: yes Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route and per model. you can slice by API key or team.
06:18 Raya: will there be a demo environment we can interact with?
06:21 Priya: we'll provision a staging tenant with sample keys and a sandbox model. staging will have limited throughput but enough for functional tests.
06:28 Tom: any embargo or NDA needed before we share sample data?
06:31 Ethan: if sample data includes PII we recommend redacting or using synthetic. we can execute a standard DPA and go from there.
06:37 Sonia: please send DPA and the pen-test checklist.
06:40 Carlos: will do.
06:42 Priya: technical note — if you plan to push very long contexts (>8k tokens) we should discuss model selection and kernel optimizations; our runtime will pick optimized kernels based on seq len. sometimes transcripts say kernal but it's kernel.
06:56 Liam: re: hardware, if we go Dedicated can we request particular GPU class?
06:59 Priya: yes you can choose pools with specific instance types subject to availability; we'll surface recommended hardware for your workload after initial evals.
07:08 Maya: team question — how disruptive is cutover from our PoC to prod? we prefer no downtime.
07:13 Ethan: with a canary rollout we can route a percentage of traffic to Redwood and gradually shift. Dedicated has capacity guarantees to avoid throttling.
07:21 Tom: okay. iiuh— excuse me — i'm also noting we have a procurement timeline; likely two weeks for initial approvals.
07:28 Ethan: that's workable. we'll aim to have pricing and SOW by end of next week.
07:34 Priya: for the pilot's dataset — please supply 200 representative prompts, and indicate 10 examples of expected correct outputs for eval.
07:43 Raya: noted.
07:45 Maya: any blockers you see on our side?
07:48 Priya: just network details and security contact for KMS handshake. once we have those, provisioning staging is straightforward.
07:56 Tom: can you run us through a very quick architecture sketch?
08:00 Priya: sure — imagine a staging VPC in your account peered to Redwood's control plane, optional private endpoints for metrics; models run on the inference plane which is either in Redwood-managed infra or in your VPC for Private. requests flow over TLS, tokenization and KV cache happen at runtime, and we export traces to your observability endpoint if you want.
08:22 Tom: got it. sound architecture.
08:26 Maya: okay let's capture the concrete dates — Carlos, can you send the calendar invite for a pilot planning session next Tue?
08:31 Carlos: yes i can do next Tue at 10am PT, i'll include a zoom link and tentative agenda.
08:37 Ethan: i'll add a tech pre-check with Priya and Liam to line up the workload.
08:41 Priya: action: i'll prepare a preliminary quantization and model-recommendation doc and a pilot runbook.
08:47 Sonia: we'll review the compliance pack once you share it.
08:50 Tom: we'll surface the CIDR and account numbers by Friday.
08:54 Ethan: excellent. any final questions?
09:00 Maya: just a small ask — can you include a simple diagram in the follow-up for our security review, and a list of exact logs exported?
09:06 Priya: yes will include architecture diagram and log schemas.
09:10 Carlos: recap of next steps now — Ethan to send onboarding checklist and SOW draft, Priya to prepare pilot runbook and model recommendations, Tom to send VPC details, Sonia to review compliance artifacts, and Carlos to schedule pilot planning.
09:28 Ethan: perfect. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs.
09:33 Maya: thanks all. bye.

Post-meeting notes: brief hiccups with audio in the middle - some words transcribed as 'kernal' and 'KV cash' but content confirmed. Pilot cadence agreed.

End of transcript.
